summary: Sravana Borkataky-Varma works in religious studies and Indology. Educated at the University of Delhi and Rice University (PhD ~2011–2016), she held posts at Harvard, Rice, the University of Montana, UNC Wilmington (~2020–2021), and the University of Houston (2023).

Sravani Kanamarlapudi specializes in linguistics and Indology. She studied at the University of Washington (2019) and pursued doctoral studies at the University of Texas at Austin (~2020) under Richard G. Salomon.

Sreeramula Rajeswara Sarma is an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. He studied at Andhra University, Visva-Bharati University, and the University of Marburg (PhD ~1963–1966), later serving as a professor at Aligarh Muslim University (~1977–1997).

Sri Anirvan (1896–1978) was a scholar in Indology and philosophy. He completed his studies at Sanskrit College and University (~1916–1918), the University of Calcutta (~1916–1920), and the University of Dhaka.

Sri Aurobindo (1872–1950) worked in philosophy, Indology, and religious studies. Educated at St Paul's School and King's College, Cambridge, he studied under Dinendra Kumar Ray and Vishnu Bhaskar Lele and held a post at Baroda (~1893–1906).

Srikanth Kaul was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. In 1967, he is attested holding positions at Government Degree College, Sopore, and as a professor at the Research and Archaeological Department, Jammu and Kashmir.

Srimanta Bhadra is a scholar in Indology, philosophy, and linguistics. Bhadra earned a PhD from Ramakrishna Mission Vivekananda Educational and Research Institute (by 2021) and served as Assistant Professor at Raja Narendra Lal Khan Women's College in 2017.

Srinivas H. Ritti (1928–2021) was an Indologist and historian. He served as an Epigraphical Assistant for the Archaeological Survey of India and Government Epigraphist for India (attested 1964–1965) and as Professor at Karnatak University (attested 1975).
Srinivasa Ayya Srinivasan (1932–2019) was an Indologist who earned his Dr. phil. at the University of Hamburg (~1961–1967). He served there as Privatdozent für Indologie from 1973 to 1997.

Srinivasa Kumar N Acharya works in Indology and philosophy. He completed an MA Vidvat-uttama Navya-nyaya at Poornaprajna Vidyapeetha and became an Assistant Professor at Manipal Academy of Higher Education in 2011.

Sriram Krishnan works in computational linguistics and Indology. Krishnan has held academic posts at Central Sanskrit University, the International Institute of Information Technology, Hyderabad, and the University of Hyderabad.

Sriram Subramanian works in Indology and computational fields. Educated at Pondicherry Engineering College, University of Cincinnati, Hindu University of America (PhD 2019), and MIT Group of Institutions, he became Principal Software Engineer at Microsoft in 2022.

Srisa Chandra Vasu (1861–1918) was an Indologist and philosopher. After earning a BA from Government College University, Lahore (~1877–1881), he served as Vakil at Allahabad High Court (~1883), founded Panini Office (1891), and was a University of Allahabad Fellow.

Stacey Boulter is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. Boulter earned a BA from Dalhousie University (2016–2025) and an MA from McMaster University (2025), where Boulter also served as a Teaching Assistant in 2025.

Stacey Van Vleet works in Tibetology, history/archaeology, and Sinology. She studied at the University of Colorado Boulder, under Carole McGranahan and Tashi Tsering Josayma, and completed a PhD at Columbia University, where she held a post in 2013.

Stamford Raffles (1781–1826) was an administrator and scholar of history and linguistics. Employed by the East India Company (~1795–1824), he served as Chief Secretary of Prince of Wales Island (1807) and Governor of Java (~1811–1816).

Stanford E. Lehmberg (1931–2012) was a historian. He completed his PhD at the University of Cambridge under doctoral supervisor Christopher Morris (~1954–1956) and later became an emeritus professor at the University of Minnesota (~1999–2012).
Stanislao Gatti (1820–1870) was an Italian scholar of philosophy and Indology. He studied at the University of Naples Federico II and later held a post there from ~1861 to 1870.

Stanislas Guyard (1846–1884) was a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He held posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études starting in 1868 and became Professor of Arabic at the Collège de France in 1884.

Stanislas Julien (1797–1873) was a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at Collège de France under Jean-Pierre Abel-Rémusat, later serving as Collège de France's Chair of Chinese (1832–1873) and professor at INALCO (1862–1871).
